title: Validate drift diagnosis and transactional repair
description:
Complete and prove the derived-state drift diagnosis and transactional repair surface on the landed repository-state engine. The repair mechanism itself lands with Group A's materializers package; this task completes its validation behavior, hardens the ownership boundaries, and supplies the proof. This is the sole leaf accountable for container criterion REQ-06.

## Background

Persisted derived state (default rule membership, default schemas, rendered projections, managed regions) is reproducible materialization, never authority. `jit validate` must report missing or stale persisted derived state as an error without treating it as authoritative, and `jit validate --fix` must transactionally restore the exact derived state from declared configuration while preserving unrelated content.

## What to build

- `jit validate` reports missing, stale, or unexpected explicitly owned materializations as deterministic errors while effective rules remain declaration-derived; expected bytes are always recomputed from declared authorities, never read back from persisted state.
- `jit validate --fix` requests one repair delta from the shared planner, applies it through the shared storage capability, and reruns validation. It obeys the repair ownership-source matrix: authored rule content (custom rows, comments, header, order, editable policy fields) is preserved unconditionally; ambiguous ownership returns a non-repairable error, never a whole-file rewrite; obsolete generated schemas are deleted only with proven generation ownership (filename convention alone is insufficient); profile asset/region repair requires resolvable applied package/version/hash provenance.
- Idempotence: a second `--fix` after a clean repair is a no-op that samples neither identifiers nor time.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Validation derives expected state from declarations and reports deterministic drift errors for missing, stale, or unexpected explicitly owned materializations on both backends, while effective rules remain declaration-derived.
- [hard] REQ-02: validate --fix applies one ownership-safe idempotent repair delta through the shared storage capability, reruns validation clean, preserves authored rule content unconditionally, and returns non-repairable errors for ambiguous ownership instead of any whole-file rewrite.

## Constraints

- Sole engine only: no alternate renderer, serializer, capture path, or publisher; all drift and repair uses the landed `repository_state` primitives.
- Out of scope (plan D19/D20): lease credential/claim-log/claim-command redesign and worktree/data-root binding redesign.

Blast radius: repository comparison/validation/fix and the ownership-matrix suites. See `dev/active/cdc840ad-plan.md` §2 (drift error and transactional repair; repair ownership-source matrix) and plan decisions D7 and D16.
